newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures settled higher amid hopes that the so-called "stability pact" deal struck late on Friday will give the Bank of France room to lower interest rates, possibly before the end of the year.

Traders said an unexpected decline in the West German Ifo business survey reinforced expectations for easier monetary policy in Europe but a stronger-than-expected U.S. industrial production report tempered the initial optimism slightly,
Few were expecting any increase in U.S. interest rates after the Federal Reserve's monetary policy council meeting on Tuesday and some said the French central bank could cut rates tomorrow.

Economists said the Bank of France, which holds on Tuesday its penultimate monetary policy council meeting before the end of the year, may want to continue with small steady interest rate cuts in the weeks ahead.

"The outlook for the Bank of France getting back on track has come closer really since the Chirac statements last Thursday and the accord in Dublin," said Iain Lindsay, bond strategist at Credit Lyonnais.
"It's almost dead certain they'll do 15 to 20 basis points because they have that much room anyway without going below German rates," Nomura International bond strategist Sonja Gibbs.
A trader at a French brokerage said if the French central decided to proceed with rate cuts it could well move tomorrow and had no reason to wait for the Bundesbank.
The Bank of France monetary policy council meets next on December 26.

A futures trader at a large French bank was more sceptical. He said he expected the central bank to wait until the two council members due to leave at the end of the year had been replaced before cutting rates again.
March PIBOR rallied at the open to set a contract high at 96.70 but failed to hold its gains.
The spread over the equivalent Euromark contract narrowed as low as 18 basis points, below the 20 basis point gap between the French intervention rate and the German repo rate.
The two-year spread between French and German bonds came in as low as six basis points, although it was back at nine basis points late on Monday.

Traders said most of the action in bond futures trading had taken place early in the session ahead of the expiry of the December contract with technical factors and the U.S. bond market holding sway thereafter.
Traders said the fact the March contract didn't close below 128.40 was relatively positive as a weaker finish would have been more likely to provoke a correction on Tuesday morning.
"128.40 is a big level below that we've got nothing before 128.26," said one trader. Another said a close below 128.40 would have made 128.00 the next significant target.

Mark weakness after the stability pact deal allowed the franc to hang onto its gains close to the highs of the year. It traded between 3.3727 and 3.3756 against the mark, little changed from 3.3739 late on Friday.
